basis: Same-author separately reasoned proposed contract, frozen before browser adapter implementation; no original-app parity claim
ordinary: Initial /items/a read A0; clean push /items/b reads B0; native Back selects original a entry with fresh read
Edit A1; manual save captures revision 1; commit then acknowledge makes saved revision 1 without navigation

history: a -> b -> c creates distinct native entries
dirty C1 then native Back first observes /items/b while committed view is /items/c; editor is hidden during reconciliation
restore the original c entry before showing exact b traversal proposal; Cancel keeps c/C1 without write
repeat Back and Discard opens original b entry; Forward opens original c entry with a fresh read, without restoring discarded C1
Back then push a truncates forward c; duplicate a URLs have distinct entry keys
departure: dirty A1; propose push b; Save captures payload/revision/proposal
replace departure by replace c while write pending; replay old cancel leaves current proposal intact
commit/ack old save records A1 version2 but stays a and cannot release c
fresh Save choice on clean revision replaces current entry with c, retaining its key
cancel departure during save; new edit A2; commit/ack captured A1 leaves A2 dirty and never navigates
fresh departure then edit again invalidates non-cancel choice
session: expire during save clears editor/proposal, marks write unknown and replaces current native entry with new epoch
re-login same owner starts fresh read; explicit Restore recovers A1 but Save stays unresolved
late old write commits/acks its original ledger; it cannot certify current editor or change its loading/saving; replay stays blocked by newer receipt/base conflict
switch to b/x with old reads/writes pending; old read success/error/finalizer and old write success/error cannot change b/x editor/status/pending operations
Back into obsolete a/x epoch restores current b/x entry without read, editor leak or old approval

limits: one disposable tab/origin per independent case
no real authentication, persistence, reload/unload guarantees, service enforcement or assistive-technology claim
unexpected foreign entry fails closed; browser traversal is reconciliation, not pre-commit veto
